*Mahantaraduka, Sanidassanattika* (Patthana 21.52) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Within the intricate analytical framework of the collection, this text investigates conditional relations by cross-combining categories from the *Mahantaraduka* (the "Great Intermediate Dyads") with the *Sanidassanattika* (the "Visible-Object Triads") [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
Reflecting the highly recursive and structural character of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text exhibits extensive textual reuse across the canonical corpus. According to DharmaNexus analysis, it shares 1,110 passages with 107 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal parallels occur within related combinatorial sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, most notably *Piṭṭhiduka, Sanidassanattika* (Patthana 21.55, sharing 142 matches including §8.1–24.1_0 ↔ §15.1–25.1), *Saññojanādichagocchaka, Sanidassanattika* (Patthana 21.51), and *Hetuduka, Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 24.6) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-tradition alignments, DharmaNexus detects five low-scoring algorithmic matches (highest score 30) with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakoṣabhāṣyaṭīkā Tattvārthā* (D4421), though these represent machine alignments rather than confirmed doctrinal or textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
